problems.memo_sentence: They report specific asymptotic resource bounds: memory-less holding times prepared with constant-depth circuits, efficient preparation of general Lévy, Poisson, compound Poisson, continuous Markov, and Cox processes with logarithmic or near-linear qubit and gate complexity in relevant parameters [C-021, C-022, C-023, C-024, C-025, C-026, C-027, C-028].
problems.source_evidence:
Theorem 1... 'τj can be prepared via a circuit consisting of ⌈log (−1/λj ln ϵ)⌉ qubits with constant circuit depth 1, and the gate complexity is ⌈log (−1/λj ln ϵ)⌉.'

Theorem 2... 'Then the Lévy process can be prepared on n log (nS) qubits within O(S + n log (nS)) circuit depth, and the gate complexity is thus O(n(S + log (nS))).'

Table 2 entries for continuous Markov, k‑order Markov, Cox, etc. give explicit polynomial expressions in n, S, λ_min, etc., not generically 'logarithmic or near‑linear' without qualification.
problems.explanation: The memo compresses a variety of distinct complexity bounds into the blanket phrase 'logarithmic or near-linear' complexity, which is not how the paper states them; some bounds include linear factors in S or S^{k+1}. This slightly overstates the general efficiency and smooths over important parameter dependencies.

problems.memo_sentence: The paper frames classical Monte Carlo for CTSPs as computationally demanding in storage and computation, motivating the quantum approach [C-010]. Relative to classical uniform sampling in time, the authors claim an exponential reduction in the required number of state-space copies, from O(T) to O(n ln τ_avg) [C-030].
problems.source_evidence: ‘The qubit number is reduced from O(T ln S) = O(nτavg ln S) of the uniform sampling method to O(n ln (τavgS)) of the QCTSP method, making an exponential reduction on the parameter τavg.’
problems.explanation: The paper explicitly compares O(T ln S) vs O(n ln(τ_avg S)) and calls this an exponential reduction in τ_avg, not simply in 'state-space copies from O(T) to O(n ln τ_avg)'. The memo’s rephrasing drops the ln S factor and changes the form of the classical scaling, overstating how cleanly the improvement can be described.

problems.memo_sentence: The information extraction procedure is presented as providing quadratic acceleration over classical counterparts for continuous-time Monte Carlo, extending quantum-enhanced Monte Carlo methods to CTSPs and enabling efficient evaluation of weighted integrals and history-sensitive quantities via flag qubits [C-006, C-018, C-019, C-031].
problems.source_evidence: In Section 4 the authors give detailed constructions, but also note trade-offs and that 'Leaving the theoretical analysis as future work, examples of option pricing and ruin theory will be given in the next section as proof of principle.' They provide complexity theorems (Theorem 7, 8) with explicit dependence on L, P, ε, etc., and acknowledge further analysis is needed.
problems.explanation: Across dimensions 3 and 4 the memo emphasizes the quadratic speedup and efficient evaluation claims from the abstract/introduction, but does not reflect that some aspects of the information-extraction analysis (especially for history-sensitive quantities) are explicitly left for future work and presented as proof-of-principle rather than fully developed performance guarantees.
